add.issue.name: TUI crashes with ERR_STRING_TOO_LONG once .epiq/log/epiq.log passes 512 MB

edit.description.md:
`logger.error` appends `new Error().stack` and `enforceLogHorizon` re-reads the whole log as one string every 50 writes. The horizon is 1000 *lines*, so lines of a few MB (see the SEA stack-frame ticket) let the file reach hundreds of MB; past Node's 512 MB string cap `readFileSync` throws inside the logger, and every later `logger.*` call takes the app down.

Seen on `~/dev/my-board`: 781 MB, 2209 lines, longest line 1.9 MB.

Fix: cap the log in bytes as well as lines, trim from the tail without decoding the whole file, and never let a logging call throw.

add.issue.name: SEA binary stack traces embed the whole base64 bundle in every frame

edit.description.md:
The SEA bootstrap loads the app with `import("data:application/javascript;base64,...")`, so V8 names the script by that URL and every stack frame carries the full ~1.9 MB bundle. One logged error is ~20 MB of log, and a crash pasted into a terminal is unreadable.

Fix: give the data-URL frames a short name (e.g. rewrite the URL to `epiq-sea` when formatting stacks) so stacks are a few hundred bytes again.

add.issue.name: Autosync retries a project with no origin remote every 15 s and logs a full stack each time

edit.description.md: On a repo without `origin`, autosync fails every tick with `fatal: origin does not appear to be a git repository` and logs it through `logger.error` with a stack. It fills the log (see the ERR_STRING_TOO_LONG ticket) and gains nothing: the failure is permanent until a remote is added. Log it once, then stop autosync or back off until the remote exists.

add.issue.name: TUI boot blocks on git pull before drawing anything

edit.description.md:
`loadProject` awaits `git pull --ff-only` on the state worktree before the first frame renders. On this board that is ~700 of ~800 ms boot; on a slow network it is seconds of blank terminal. Import cost and event replay are both under 200 ms.

Fix: materialise the local event log and render immediately, then pull in the background under the sync lock and reload state only if the pull moved HEAD. Sync pill shows the pull while it runs.

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: PR #244, commit 02b77009. `loadProject` no longer awaits the pull; it materialises the local log and renders, then `refreshProjectFromRemote` pulls after the first frame under the sync lock and reloads only if HEAD moved. Pill shows `...` while pulling, then `Pulled` / `Already synced` / `off` / `---`. A clone with no init event in its log still pulls first. `:open` gets the same. Measured against an unreachable origin: main draws the board after 75 s, this branch after 0.23 s.

Deviation from the description: the empty-log guard checks for an `init.workspace` event rather than for zero events; a fresh clone already holds a contributor registration, which cannot boot alone.
add.issue.comment.author: HVK8KMV924DBNFBDQV8RCZ9S06

add.issue.name: Sync in flight during :open reloads the old project over the new one

edit.description.md:
Found reviewing PR #244 (branch worktree-2KBWD7E-boot-pull-background).

`syncAndReloadState` resolves the state branch root from `process.cwd()` when it starts, then reloads the board from that root after the network wait. `:open` chdirs to another project mid-sync, so an autosync (or `:sync`) that was waiting on the remote when the user opened project B materialises project A's log over B's board.

The boot-time pull in PR #244 guards against this with an `isCurrentProject` check after the pull; the sync path needs the same check before its reload.

add.issue.comment.md:
Self-review for boot flow and multi-agent use, amended into the same commit:

- The boot pull now reuses `pullBranchRebaseIfPresent` (fetch + rebase with autostash) instead of `git pull --ff-only`. A board whose state branch was never pushed is skipped quietly rather than flagged; local unpushed commits and uncommitted event lines are handled the way a sync handles them; no shared FETCH_HEAD hazard between processes.
- A pull still in flight when `:open` switched projects no longer reloads the old project over the new one. The sync path on main has the same race; filed as 0YC23TC.
- Other processes (MCP agents, GUI) are untouched: they boot via `epiq-api` with `pull: false`. The boot pull takes the sync lock, so it skips when another process holds the worktree, and autosync skips while the boot pull holds it.

Known gap: if the user is mid-edit when the pull lands, the reload is skipped and the pill shows `idle`, as autosync does; the next sync applies it.

Stress run (960k events) matches main within noise. Unit, e2e and gate all green.
add.issue.comment.author: HVK8KMV924DBNFBDQV8RCZ9S06

add.issue.name: GUI board freezes after a failed autosync: broadcast lives only in the sync success branch

edit.description.md:
Reported 2026-09-06: the GUI seems to stop updating when the remote sync fails. Code reading confirms a mechanism.

`source/gui/api/lib/api-autosync.ts` (~66-79) is the only path that broadcasts state to every connected client while live, and it sits behind two guards: `if (isFail(result)) return;` and `if (!pulled && !createdCommit && !bootstrapped) return;`.

- A sync whose pull succeeded but whose push failed (auth, rejected) returns fail, so the events already rebased into the worktree are never broadcast.
- `pulled` is HEAD movement only, so on later ticks nothing is new and the guard suppresses the broadcast even after the remote recovers. The board stays at pre-failure state until reconnect or a `state:get`.
- Mutations from one GUI socket are answered to that socket only (`websocket.ts` `sendStateAfterMutation`), so other windows also go stale.
- Secondary: a sync failure renders as `-` in the header with the message in a tooltip, so the stall is nearly invisible.

Fix direction: broadcast on the log signature changing (`log-signature.ts`) rather than on git HEAD movement, and broadcast after a failed sync too when the pull moved the worktree.

add.issue.comment.md: Reproduced end to end: GUI on clone A with autosync, clone B pushes a ticket via the MCP binary, then the remote's pre-receive hook rejects pushes. Unfixed main: bob's ticket lands in A's worktree log but no `state` frame ever reaches the client. Fix on branch `8SFXCJC-gui-sync-broadcast`: the tick compares the log signature against the one last published and broadcasts on any difference, regardless of the sync result; the frame arrives on the tick whose push failed. Header now says "sync failed" instead of `-`.
add.issue.comment.author: HVK8KMV924DBNFBDQV8RCZ9S06

add.issue.comment.md: Solution: merged via PR #251 (commits 82499e0d, bf7c4e76). `api-autosync.ts` no longer decides the broadcast from the sync result or from git HEAD moving. Each pass compares the event-log signature (`log-signature.ts`) against the one it last attempted and, on any difference, derives and broadcasts state whatever `sync()` returned — so a pull followed by a refused push, a remote coming back, or another process appending to the worktree all reach every client. The signature is taken before the derive, so a line landing mid-derivation costs one extra broadcast rather than a missed one; a log that fails to derive is retried only once it changes. The project root is resolved upward, so a GUI launched from a subdirectory still broadcasts. Header shows "sync failed" instead of `-`. Verified with a two-clone reproduction against the real server (fails on the old main, passes now) and `api-autosync.test.ts`.

add.issue.name: mcp/api: a shared bootForWrite would remove the 9-line boot/actor/state preamble from 21 call sites

add.issue.name: Duplicated helpers the file splits made visible: persist-root, resolveRepoRoot, ticket tag/assignee projection, the tags.ts target loop

edit.description.md:
Found reviewing PR #246. All four predate the split, which only moved them into their own files where they now read as deliberate abstractions.

- `commands/persist-root.ts` unwraps `getPersistRoot` (`lib/storage/paths.ts`) and re-wraps it with the same success message, so it is a no-op. Three siblings (`move.cmd.ts`, `edit.cmd.ts`, `new.cmd.ts`) call `getPersistRoot` directly, so the directory now has two ways to ask one question.
- `resolveRepoRoot` exists byte-identically in `mcp/api/boot.ts` and `mcp/epiq-time-travel.ts`. Importing either way would cycle; the fix is a single home in `lib/storage/paths.ts` beside `resolveClosestEpiqProjectRoot`.
- `mcp/api/issue-projection.ts`'s `getIssueTags` / `getIssueAssignees` repeat `getTicketTags` / `getTicketAssignees` from `lib/utils/ticket.utils.ts`, differing only by adding `color`. `TicketListItem.tsx` uses the lib helper, so this is the third site.
- `mcp/api/tags.ts` `addIssueTag` hand-rolls the body of `forEachTarget`, which it already imports from `issue-targets.ts`; `issues.ts` calls the shared helper in both its equivalents.

Also: `delete.cmd.ts` hand-writes a type guard re-declaring the `add.issue.comment` payload instead of using `isAddCommentEvent` (`lib/utils/comment.utils.ts`) over the canonical `AppEvent` generic, so it will go stale silently if the payload changes.

add.issue.name: App.tsx hands 27 hook return values down as individual props; the two new hooks could be called where they are used

edit.description.md:
Found reviewing PR #246. The TPK9N0T extraction moved the bodies out of `App.tsx` but left the wiring, so App destructures the hooks' 27 return fields and forwards them one prop at a time.

- `useIssueMutations` returns 17 fields; App destructures all of them and passes 16 to children, matched by 16 prop declarations in `IssueDetails`. Roughly 50 lines exist only to move the value down one level. `IssueDetails` already imports `AttachmentUploadStatus` from the hook's module, so it could call the hook itself and App would pass `send` and `setState` only.
- `useSwimlaneEditing` returns 10 fields, three of them raw `useState` setters, and App writes the hook's private `{swimlaneId, title}` shape itself. An interface of `{openCreate, openRename, requestDelete, modals}` would encapsulate it. Its `selectedBoard` argument also round-trips: it is passed in only so `deletingSwimlane` can be derived and returned.

Also in the same area: `diffStyle`, `onAddComment`, `onFileTicket` and `comments` are declared in `IssueCommits`, `CommitRow` and `FileRow` and forwarded untouched, so one new diff-selection callback costs six coordinated edits.

add.issue.name: Show how long tickets have sat in a lane: dwell time in the swimlane header, a clock on the stuck cards

edit.description.md:
A board says what is where, never how long it has been there — so a ticket parked in Review for three weeks looks exactly like one that arrived this morning.

**Swimlane header:** a dwell figure beside the ticket count, `Review (5) · 23h`. No colour on it. Live mode only — a dwell measured against wall-clock "now" is meaningless while the timeline is scrubbed.

**Cards:** a clock icon, amber then red, on the tickets that have sat far longer than their own lane's other tickets. Relative to the lane, not to the board: Backlog is structurally the oldest column and a board-wide comparison would light it up permanently.

**Where the number comes from:** every node already carries its own `log` in materialized state. Replaying `payload.parent` over it gives the moment the ticket last entered its current lane — a move that only reorders within the lane keeps the same parent and so does not reset the clock. No new event type, no schema change, no log rescan.

**Decisions taken** (see comments): median not mean for the header figure; outlier thresholds relative to the lane median with an absolute floor; closed tickets excluded; negative dwell clamped to zero, since ULID times come from whichever machine authored the move.

GUI only. The TUI draws its own lane headers and can pick the same derivation up later.

add.issue.name: A swimlane's own stats panel: dwell, where tickets come from and go next, and what the lane's code did

edit.description.md:
`Y34SCVN` put a lane's dwell figures in the swimlane header. A header is the wrong size for what there is to say about a lane, so the figures move into the inspector behind a stats icon on the header, and take company with them.

**Replaces** the `6d med · 3w max` text `Y34SCVN` added. The header keeps its title, count and lock, and gains a stats icon; the figures live in the panel.

**The panel**, in the inspector beside `IssueDetails` and `BulkDetails`, reusing the `issue-stats.style` vocabulary the ticket Stats tab already draws with:

- When the lane was created, from its own ULID.
- Dwell: median, average, longest — the figures the header was carrying.
- **Usually arrives from** — the lanes tickets were in before this one, ranked, with shares. Not a single "most common": a 51/49 split says something a winner-takes-all line hides.
- **Usually moves on to** — the same, forwards. Tickets sitting in the lane now have no next yet and are excluded from that count rather than counted as staying.
- Commits across the lane's tickets, and the diff they add up to (`+932 −234`).

**Where the data comes from:** every node's `log` gives the sequence of lanes it has been in — the same walk `Y34SCVN` added for lane entry, generalised to the whole sequence, so one rule answers "when did it arrive", "where did it come from" and "where did it go". Commits come through `getIssueStats`, per ticket, aggregated — so the panel is fetched on demand over the socket like issue detail is, never on the broadcast path.

Depends on `Y34SCVN` (PR #276). Related: `PLW4HRR`, whose fix is the same shared walk.

add.issue.name: The ticket Stats tab's time-in-lane restarts when a card is reordered inside its own column

edit.description.md:
`deriveBoardStats` (`source/lib/stats/board-stats.ts`) sets the arrival time on every move naming the current lane:

```
if (event.parentId === currentLaneId) landedInCurrentAt = event.t;
```

Dragging a card up or down inside its own column is a `move.node` carrying the lane it is already in, so it overwrites the arrival time and the Stats tab's "in lane" figure drops to zero. Tidying a column silently erases how long everything in it has been waiting — the one number that says a ticket is stuck.

Same function, second divergence: it only reads `move.node`, so a `reopen.issue` — which also changes the parent — is invisible, and a reopened ticket's figure falls back to its creation date instead of the moment it came back.

**Repro:** open a ticket that has sat in a lane for days, read Stats; drag it one place up in the same column; read Stats again. Days becomes seconds.

**Fix:** the rule already exists correctly in `laneEntryTime` (`source/lib/utils/lane-dwell.ts`, from `Y34SCVN`), which compares the parent rather than counting moves and reads every event that carries one. Both should read one shared walk rather than two implementations of the same idea that disagree — which is also what `MR1Y0AP` needs for its arrives-from/moves-on-to figures.

add.issue.name: A stay curve in every swimlane header, at the weight of the border

edit.description.md:
`MR1Y0AP` put the lane's stay trend in a panel one click away. The shape of that curve is worth having without the click — whether a column is climbing is the kind of thing you want to catch out of the corner of an eye while looking at something else.

A sparkline in each swimlane header, drawn in `GUI_THEME.line` — the border's own colour. No axis, no numbers, no labels, no hover, no hit target. It brightens with the column's proximity glow as the pointer approaches, and hides while the board is scrubbed like every other figure measured against now.

**Sharing the glow rather than imitating it.** `Panel` gains an optional render-prop form handing its children the glow strength it is drawing the border at, so the curve lights up *with* the frame instead of running a second window-wide pointer listener per column. The border's glow also falls off radially from the pointer; at 56px against a 200px radius that gradient is invisible, so the sparkline takes only the part that reads.

**Where the data comes from.** A new `board:stay-trends:get` returns every lane's curve in one answer — fetched once per board, deliberately not on the broadcast path, and no git at all, unlike the panel's code figures.

**And the derivation had to get cheaper first.** `deriveLaneStayTrend` asked every lane about every ticket on every day, so cost grew as lanes × days × tickets × visits — fine for one panel, not for every header. Driven from the visits instead (a stay already knows the run of days it covers) it is one pass. Measured: 150 tickets / 6 lanes 4.7ms → 0.7ms; 500 / 10 8.6ms → 1.4ms; 2000 / 12 46.3ms → 5.4ms. The existing tests passed unchanged against the rewrite, which is what says it is the same answer.

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: PR #279, branch `worktree-SJVQR7H-lane-sparkline`.

Two things came back from review and both were real.

**The fragments.** Breaking the line across empty days is right in the panel and wrong at 56px — three disconnected strokes read as a glitch. The header draws only the most recent unbroken run, which is one clean curve and also the only stretch a glance is asking about.

**The glow, first attempt.** A `Panel` render prop recreates its children on every pointer sample, so every card in every column re-rendered ~60 times a second while the mouse moved — six columns, six listeners, six subtree re-renders per sample. Replaced with a CSS variable (`PANEL_GLOW_VAR`): the panel publishes the strength it is drawing its border at, the sparkline reads it in `calc()`, React never hears about the pointer, and children stay referentially stable. Confirmed live — with the pointer over the second column the four lanes reported `0.35, 1, 0, 0`.

Noted honestly: the re-render fix is structural rather than measured. I reasoned it from how React treats a recreated children tree and did not benchmark the janky version before removing it.

The gate failed once on `source/test/e2e/edit-scope.e2e.test.ts` — a TUI editor-picker timeout in the container suite. Nothing here goes near the TUI, and the same tree passed on the next run.
add.issue.comment.author: HVK8KMV924DBNFBDQV8RCZ9S06

add.issue.comment.md:
Second review pass, and one of these was a real misreading on my part.

**Proximity, not presence.** I had been publishing the panel's glow *strength*, so the curve went fully lit whenever the pointer was anywhere on that column. The border's glow is a radial gradient centred on the cursor — it lights where you are, not everywhere on the panel. The sparkline now measures its own distance to the pointer with the same falloff and reach. Verified: beside the curve `0.87`, 600px down the same column `0`, other lanes `0`.

`Panel.tsx` is back to untouched as a result — the render prop is gone and so is the CSS variable that replaced it, since measuring from the curve needs neither. The opacity is still written straight to the node, so a pointer sample re-renders nothing.

**Smoothing took two changes, not one.** A Catmull-Rom spline passes through every reading, so one busy afternoon spiking a day's median still drew an EKG at 56px. A three-day rolling mean before the spline leaves the shape and drops the twitch.

Also: both ends fade out via a stroke gradient, the curve moved right of the stats button, and the lit copy is down to 0.3 against the border's 0.41.
add.issue.comment.author: HVK8KMV924DBNFBDQV8RCZ9S06

add.issue.comment.md:
Third pass, and it turned up a real bug rather than a taste call.

A lone curve in a header reads as a mark on the screen, so it needed a frame. Two candidates: a grid (baseline plus week uprights) and an L of axes. The axes win at this size — uprights crossing a curve in a 14px box are clutter, not context.

**The axes then stopped rendering entirely, and I reported them as merely faint.** An SVG gradient in the default `objectBoundingBox` units is not painted when the bounding box has zero width or height, and a straight axis is exactly that — so giving them the curve's fade silently deleted both. The curve was unaffected because its own box has two dimensions. Fixed with `gradientUnits="userSpaceOnUse"` and explicit coordinates.

Worth recording how it was caught: a 3× screenshot was ambiguous enough that I read what I expected to see. A 10× element capture settled it in one look. Zoom, do not squint.

Weights, after the same misreading twice: the axes are `dim2` at 0.35, not the border's `line` at 0.15 — that alpha carries a whole column's edge and vanishes in a 56px L. The curve is `dim2` at 0.8, clearly above its frame and still a hint. Each axis fades toward its own outer edge only; the corner stays solid, since that is what anchors the L.

add.issue.name: A tooltip of our own: fast, black, monospace, and not clipped by the panel it sits in

edit.description.md:
The GUI leans on the browser's own `title` tooltip in about 110 places. It waits roughly a second, cannot be styled, and renders in OS chrome that looks like nothing else here.

A `Tooltip` of our own: pitch black, the app's own mono, a ~150ms delay and an 80ms fade. Fast enough to feel like part of the app rather than something the operating system decided to show.

**No typing animation.** It was considered and dropped: a tooltip is summoned because somebody does not know something, so animating it buys back the latency the whole change exists to remove — and a tooltip fires dozens of times an hour, which is exactly where repeated delight turns into friction. The app's terminal character comes from genuinely being mono and dense; a typing effect would simulate a terminal beside the real thing.

**The one piece of new infrastructure is a portal.** `Panel` sets `overflow: hidden`, so a tooltip inside a swimlane column is clipped by the column. It has to render at `document.body`, and nothing in the GUI portals today.

**Adopted where it earns its place, not swept across all 110 `title`s.** An icon-only trigger that relied on `title` for its accessible name needs an explicit `aria-label` when its tooltip moves here — the native attribute was doing two jobs.

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: PR #280, merged as `644615d2`.

`TooltipLayer` is mounted once and listens at the document, so all ~110 existing `title` attributes are covered without a single call site changing — and so is every one written afterwards. Wrapping each trigger was the first attempt and was the wrong shape: an enormous diff that new code would immediately start bypassing.

The attribute has to come off while the tooltip is up, since there is no way to keep `title` and suppress the native bubble. Two rules follow, both found by running the suite rather than by reasoning:

- **Strip when the tooltip appears, not when the pointer lands.** Taking it early broke `getByTitle('Edit comment')` in `comments.pw.ts` — a locator re-resolving mid-hover could no longer find the element. The native bubble waits a second, so there was never a race to win.
- **Focus never strips.** Browsers draw the native bubble on hover only, so there was nothing to suppress on keyboard focus, and removing `title` there deleted a button's accessible name at the moment a screen reader would read it. No test would have caught that.

Delay is 500ms, half the browser's, at the user's call — the first cut was 150ms and read as too eager.

Also `title="Show commits"` on the Code checkbox, which sat beside the board series' "Show board events" with nothing to say.

Three Playwright tests in `source/test/e2e-gui/tooltip.pw.ts`; full browser suite 156 passing.
